records.description: The reviewed KamLAND reactor disappearance, SNO active-flavor transformation, Super-Kamiokande atmospheric disappearance and OPERA accelerator tau-appearance results support flavor change compatible with their declared oscillation models across different preparations and responses. Their counts, fluxes, averaged probabilities and conditional fit parameters are distinct observables. This synthesis preserves those boundaries and supplies neither a pooled transition probability nor a new global fit.
records.name: Neutrino oscillation evidence across preparations
openObligations: This is a literature synthesis of already admitted results. Each chain retains its acquisition, selection, adopted flux/cross sections, detector response, backgrounds and inference contexts. Counts are not event-level oscillation probabilities. Reused events, multiple summaries and alternative fits within an acquisition are dependent; this synthesis is not another independent experiment or combined significance.

KamLAND reactor antineutrinos involve changing reactor histories and baselines. The reported period-averaged survival and historical two-flavor rate-and-shape fit use response and background models; the 180 km display baseline is not a single experimental baseline. Shape-only, KamLAND-only and solar-combined fits are distinct, and the solar combination adds a CPT assumption.

SNO reports a joint electron versus combined muon-plus-tau active-flux inference under its B8-shape and weak-response assumptions. This is not a measured oscillation phase, separate muon/tau identification or unique proof of adiabatic MSW conversion. Subtracting channel-flux centers does not reproduce its covariance, joint result or significance; the SK-added and shape-relaxed analyses remain separate.

Super-Kamiokande uses atmospheric flux, zenith distributions and detector/kinematic proxies with a historical two-flavor fit. The 1998 disappearance analysis does not directly identify tau appearance or distinguish its tau interpretation from the stated sterile alternative. Its L/E cross-check reuses the sample and does not resolve an oscillation dip.

OPERA reconstructs tau candidates in a primarily muon-neutrino beam using channel-dependent efficiencies and backgrounds. Its calibrated channel-combination significance, signal strength and full-mixing mass-squared compatibility reuse the same candidate sample. Dividing five candidates by an interaction total does not produce an oscillation probability, and the Fisher-product statistic is not the calibrated tail probability.

Historical effective two-flavor parameters, confidence constructions and adopted external inputs retain their publication-specific meanings; no current three-flavor global fit is inferred. These results do not establish absolute neutrino masses, every individual mass to be nonzero, Dirac/Majorana character, a unique mass-generation mechanism or quantitative astrophysical/cosmological transport.

limitations: This is a literature synthesis of already admitted results. Each chain retains its acquisition, selection, adopted flux/cross sections, detector response, backgrounds and inference contexts. Counts are not event-level oscillation probabilities. Reused events, multiple summaries and alternative fits within an acquisition are dependent; this synthesis is not another independent experiment or combined significance.

KamLAND reactor antineutrinos involve changing reactor histories and baselines. The reported period-averaged survival and historical two-flavor rate-and-shape fit use response and background models; the 180 km display baseline is not a single experimental baseline. Shape-only, KamLAND-only and solar-combined fits are distinct, and the solar combination adds a CPT assumption.

SNO reports a joint electron versus combined muon-plus-tau active-flux inference under its B8-shape and weak-response assumptions. This is not a measured oscillation phase, separate muon/tau identification or unique proof of adiabatic MSW conversion. Subtracting channel-flux centers does not reproduce its covariance, joint result or significance; the SK-added and shape-relaxed analyses remain separate.

Super-Kamiokande uses atmospheric flux, zenith distributions and detector/kinematic proxies with a historical two-flavor fit. The 1998 disappearance analysis does not directly identify tau appearance or distinguish its tau interpretation from the stated sterile alternative. Its L/E cross-check reuses the sample and does not resolve an oscillation dip.

OPERA reconstructs tau candidates in a primarily muon-neutrino beam using channel-dependent efficiencies and backgrounds. Its calibrated channel-combination significance, signal strength and full-mixing mass-squared compatibility reuse the same candidate sample. Dividing five candidates by an interaction total does not produce an oscillation probability, and the Fisher-product statistic is not the calibrated tail probability.

Historical effective two-flavor parameters, confidence constructions and adopted external inputs retain their publication-specific meanings; no current three-flavor global fit is inferred. These results do not establish absolute neutrino masses, every individual mass to be nonzero, Dirac/Majorana character, a unique mass-generation mechanism or quantitative astrophysical/cosmological transport.

These results support mass-induced flavor mixing within their stated models, while preserving distinct observables, preparations and inference assumptions.
records.name: Scoped neutrino mass and mixing evidence
openObligations: KamLAND contributes its reactor-only rate-and-shape two-flavor fit; its shape-only and CPT-assuming solar-combined analyses are not new reactor acquisitions. The 1998 Super-Kamiokande atmospheric fit is a historical effective two-flavor result conditioned on flux, response and nuisance assumptions; it did not directly distinguish tau from sterile disappearance. Their reported characteristic splitting scales are not relabeled as exact modern three-state eigenpairs or combined into a new likelihood.

The SNO-only direct joint electron/non-electron active-flux inference supports solar flavor transformation under its B8-shape and response assumptions. It is not NC-minus-CC subtraction of independent fluxes, a separate muon/tau identification, an oscillation-phase or mass-splitting measurement, or proof of a unique matter-enhanced mechanism. Its SK-added solar constraint is not the distinct 1998 atmospheric exposure.

OPERA appearance significance, signal strength and its full-mixing mass-squared interval reuse the same 2008-2012 acquisition, channel counts and response. The compatibility result is not independent appearance replication or a third distinct oscillation frequency. Its adopted nominal splitting and full-mixing inputs are not additional fitted observations; the reported intervals and significance retain their original confidence construction.

These are four named inference contexts and five outcomes, not five independent experiments or a global three-flavor fit. Event selections, intermediate summaries, alternative analysis implementations and fitted outputs within a campaign share data. No likelihood, nuisance covariance, combined parameter range, mass ordering or confidence coverage is newly reconstructed.

Within a supplied common three-state mass-induced interpretation, distinct nonzero splitting scales motivate the formal identifiability consequence of at least two nonzero masses. This comparison does not independently establish all assumptions of that embedding or measure all three masses, an absolute scale, Dirac/Majorana nature, Majorana phases, sterile content or a unique mechanism. The formal common-shift invariance is not a new experimental bound.

Generic solar, atmospheric, reactor and accelerator evidence placeholders are restricted to these actual admitted sources and analysis stages. Astrophysical/cosmological constraints, beta endpoints, neutrinoless double beta decay and universal parent/formation/maintenance claims remain excluded from this finite evidence comparison.

limitations: A charged-current flavor label is tied to the accompanying charged-lepton preparation/readout; it is not an individual propagation mass, a classical mixture measured simultaneously in two bases or a guarantee that every neutrino state exhibits flavor oscillation. Closed three-active unitarity is a supplied model restriction, not an exclusion of every additional state or nonunitary effective submatrix.

The minimal renormalizable Standard Model with its stated field content has no neutrino mass term. Charged-fermion Higgs/Yukawa relations do not automatically supply neutrino masses. Alternative massive-neutrino field/operator assignments are formal inputs, not a measured Dirac/Majorana choice, a unique origin or a prediction of mixing parameters.

At fixed mixing, baseline and energy in the declared leading coherent ultrarelativistic vacuum phase, an admissible common mass-squared shift leaves oscillation probabilities unchanged. Two unequal nonzero mass-squared differences from a shared reference imply three distinct eigenvalues and at least two positive masses, not three positive masses. Equal nonzero differences are not sufficient for that conclusion. Selected effective two-flavor fits are not automatically exact three-state eigenpair measurements.

Oscillation evidence here does not determine an absolute mass scale, the mass ordering beyond its selected conditional models, Dirac/Majorana character, Majorana phases, sterile content or the origin of the mixing/Yukawa parameters. No beta-endpoint, neutrinoless-double-beta, cosmological mass-sum or modern global-fit bounds are imported.

Propagation, coherence and applications retain the separate scope of card 1.17. The matter Hamiltonian uses vacuum masses/mixing as inputs; its medium potential does not generate those vacuum masses. Source composition, collisions, self-refraction, cosmic expansion and detector response require their own quantitative transport inputs. This admission supplies no astrophysical transport or cosmological prediction.

The original necessary lepton parent is retained only as a descriptive flavor-readout/model dependency. Weight 1, Nmin=Ncrit=1, arising/maintenance and direction/interaction codes do not establish a measured formation threshold, universal causal necessity or temporal emergence sequence. SOMA phase 1, property/type-role 3 and the established label are not scientific evidence.

The original refusal to specify a deeper mass-generation mechanism is preserved. Finite evidence for mass-induced mixing under declared assumptions does not require selecting a speculative mechanism; it also does not validate every flavor-transformation explanation or a universal sector-wide construction.
